reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis relies on in-situ formation of MoS₂ in ambient air up to 800 °C, which contradicts the well-known oxidation of MoS₂ above ~350–400 °C, making the proposed mechanism physically unsound.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification experiment is clear and well-defined, with specific measurements and a decisive criterion, though the impracticality of the hypothesis itself makes the test moot.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a mechanism (MoS₂ lubrication at 800 °C in air) that is fundamentally flawed, so testing it would not advance understanding of high-temperature tribology.
